findings.evidence: 'Rank them by observable consequence and evidence strength; a demonstrated trade-off beats a neat principle match.' There is no tie-break when a success candidate and a warning candidate are equally strong, but the Load rule (line 13) loads anti-patterns.md only when the lesson is a warning, so two runs can pick different lessons and load different files
findings.fix: Add one clause to step 2: 'On a tie, prefer the candidate with test evidence; if both have it, lead with what the change got right and give the warning as the Also worth noting line (read anti-patterns.md for it).'

findings.evidence: Six evals cover a casual question, a pasted diff, a rename, a range, untracked files and no changes. None covers the feature-branch base detection (symbolic-ref, then main/master, then the last-5 fallback) or the merge-commit gotcha ('git show <merge> prints a combined diff that is empty for a clean merge'). Eval 'casual-reflection' also lists references/se-principles.md under files, but that is a skill file, not an input
findings.fix: Add an eval with a fixture git log showing a clean merge commit that asserts the answer uses --first-parent evidence and does not report 'no changes', plus one where the repo has no origin/HEAD and only a master branch, asserting the stated base is master. Drop references/se-principles.md from the casual-reflection files list

findings.evidence: 'Feature branch (default off the base branch) | Base: `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`...'. Followed the branch: nothing says how to tell whether HEAD is on the base branch (for example by comparing `git branch --show-current` with the base), and a detached HEAD (CI checkout, mid-rebase) matches neither the feature-branch row nor the base-branch rule on line 27
findings.fix: Add to the scope paragraph: 'Compare `git branch --show-current` with the base; an empty result means detached HEAD: use `git log -p --first-parent -n 5` and say the HEAD was detached.'
